newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: France supports Russia on strengthening OSCE.
newsitem.headline: France supports Russia on strengthening OSCE.

text.p: France gave support to Russian demands for a major strengthening of Europe's biggest security organisation at a summit on Monday, despite opposition from many other states suspicious of Moscow's intentions.

French President Jacques Chirac told leaders from more than 50 nations at a security summit in Lisbon that the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) should be strengthened by a formal treaty or charter.
Chirac said the organisation should also be given a firmer legal basis.
"Seven years after the fall of the Berlin Wall, we have an historic opportunity to...rebuild the European family," said Chirac.

Russia, which fears it will be isolated when NATO takes on new members from Eastern Europe, wants to strengthen the OSCE as a counterbalance to the Western alliance -- with real authority over other organisations in Europe. Russia is a leading member of the 54-nation forum.

France and Germany have shown some sympathy for Russian concerns, but many other NATO allies and many other countries fear Russia wants to gain an effective veto on important European security issues by changing the way the OSCE works.
U.S. Vice President Al Gore took this line when he told the summit the organisation should remain flexible and work with NATO -- not compete with it or give it orders.
"The OSCE does not need to be transformed into the only orchestrating institution of European security," said Gore.
